title: Pattern Headings: Art
summary: Pattern-heading list for art. Covers headings for individual art forms in the fine arts and for art and art forms qualified by nationality, region, ethnic group, or time period; excludes Art itself, headings qualified by religion, decorative arts, performing arts, and architecture. Gives period subdivisions (general list established under Art, Italian; separate lists for Chinese, Japanese and Korean art) that are not free-floating under unqualified art forms or art forms qualified by period, plus topical and form subdivisions usable after period subdivisions.
validation_rules: Subdivisions on this list are free-floating under headings for individual art forms in the fine arts and for art and art forms qualified by nationality, region, ethnic group, or time period (e.g. *Drawing*; *Art, French*; *Painting, German*; *Iron sculpture, Japanese*; *Sculpture, Southeast Asian*; *Arts, Māori*; *Hispanic American art*; *Landscape painting, Medieval*; *Sculpture, Modern*). (H 1148 sec. B)

The category does not include the heading *Art*, headings qualified by religion (e.g. *Buddhist art*), or headings for the decorative arts (e.g. *Pottery*), performing arts (e.g. *Theater*), or architecture (e.g. *Architecture, Modern*); list subdivisions are usable under these only if allowed by other instruction sheets or established editorially. (H 1148 sec. C)
A listed subdivision may be used free-floating under any heading in the category if appropriate and no conflict exists in the subject authority file. (H 1148 sec. D)

Period subdivisions on this list are not free-floating under unqualified headings for art forms (e.g. *Drawing*) nor under headings for art forms qualified by time period (e.g. *Sculpture, Modern*); they require a national, regional, or ethnic qualifier. (H 1148 sec. F)

General period subdivisions `--10th century` through `--21st century` (`--10th century`, `--11th century`, ... `--20th century`, `--21st century`) may be used under art and art forms of all nations, regions, and ethnic groups except China, Japan, and Korea. (H 1148 sec. F.1)

Under art forms qualified by *Chinese*, use only: `--To 221 B.C.`; `--Qin-Han dynasties, 221 B.C.-220 A.D.`; `--Three kingdoms-Sui dynasty, 220-618`; `--Tang-Five dynasties, 618-960`; `--Song-Yuan dynasties, 960-1368`; `--Ming-Qing dynasties, 1368-1912`; `--20th century`; `--21st century`. (H 1148 sec. F.2)

Under art forms qualified by *Japanese*, use only: `--To 794`; `--To 1600`; `--To 1868`; `--Heian period, 794-1185`; `--Kamakura-Momoyama periods, 1185-1600`; `--Edo period, 1600-1868`; `--19th century`; `--1868-`; `--Meiji period, 1868-1912`; `--20th century`; `--Taishō period, 1912-1926`; `--21st century`. (H 1148 sec. F.3)

Under art forms qualified by *Korean*, use only: `--To 935`; `--To 1900`; `--Koryŏ period, 935-1392`; `--Chosŏn dynasty, 1392-1910`; `--19th century`; `--20th century`; `--21st century`. (H 1148 sec. F.4)
If a general period subdivision is inappropriate for a specific heading, the appropriate subdivision must be established under that specific heading (not free-floating). (H 1148 sec. F.1)
Topical and form subdivisions on this list may follow free-floating or established period subdivisions (e.g. *Painting, French--19th century--Themes, motives*), except as noted. (H 1148 sec. G)
`--Foreign influences` is not valid after a period subdivision. (H 1148 sec. G)
Additional subdivisions may be used from the general free-floating list in H 1095. (H 1148 sec. G)
Only `--Appreciation`, `--Conservation and restoration`, `--Expertising`, and `--Forgeries` on this list may be subdivided geographically. (H 1148 sec. G)
Form subdivisions on this list (`--Catalogs` $v, `--Chronology` $v) remain valid LCSH. (H 1148 sec. H)
[LC practice] LC catalogers no longer use form subdivisions; they assign LCGFT terms instead. (H 1148 sec. H)

[LC practice] Establish new subdivisions under *Art, Italian* whenever possible; establish subdivisions appropriate only to Chinese, Japanese, or Korean art under *Art, Chinese*; *Art, Japanese*; or *Art, Korean*. (H 1148 sec. E)
[LC practice] If an exceptional variant form is retained, make a UF reference from the equivalent free-floating subdivision form (H 195); otherwise propose a change (H 193). (H 1148 sec. D)

sections.heading: A. Recent Revisions
sections.text: 2026-04: Updated template. Added instructions related to LCGFT implementation.

sections.heading: B. Types of headings covered
sections.text:
Headings for individual art forms in the fine arts as well as art and art forms qualified by nationality, region, ethnic group, or time period.

Examples:

```
Drawing
Art, French
Painting, German
Iron sculpture, Japanese
Sculpture, Southeast Asian
Arts, Māori
Hispanic American art
Landscape painting, Medieval
Sculpture, Modern
```

sections.heading: C. Types of headings not covered
sections.text:
The category does not include the heading *Art*, headings qualified by religion, nor headings for the decorative arts, performing arts, or architecture. The subdivisions in this list may be used for these categories if allowed by other instructions sheets or established editorially as appropriate to the topic.

Examples:

```
Buddhist art
Pottery
Theater
Architecture, Modern
```

sections.heading: D. Conflicts
sections.text:
Any subdivision listed here can be used as a free-floating subdivision under any heading belonging to the category if it is appropriate and no conflict exists in the subject authority file.

Subject authority records may exist for headings employing variant phrases or subdivisions equivalent to subdivisions on this list.

LC practice: If an exceptional variant form is to be retained, make a UF reference from the equivalent free-floating subdivision form following the procedures in H 195 if the reference does not yet exist. Otherwise, submit a proposal to change the variant form along with all bibliographic records requiring correction following the procedures in H 193.

sections.heading: E. New subdivisions
sections.text: Establish new subdivisions under *Art, Italian* whenever possible. Establish subdivisions appropriate only to the art of China, Japan, or Korea under *Art, Chinese*; *Art, Japanese*; or *Art, Korean*.

sections.heading: F. Period subdivisions
sections.text: Note: These period subdivisions are not free-floating under unqualified headings for art forms, such as *Drawing*, nor under headings for art forms qualified by time period, such as *Sculpture, Modern*.

sections.heading: G. List of topical subdivisions
sections.text:
This list of subdivisions provides free-floating subdivisions used specifically for art headings. Additional subdivisions may be used from the general list of free-floating subdivisions in H 1095. These subdivisions may be used following free-floating or established period subdivisions, except as noted below.

Note: The scope notes included below may not reflect the full text as found in Classification Web Plus, as it includes information not relevant to art headings. The copy of the scope note as found in Classification Web Plus is authoritative.

| Subdivision | May Subd Geog | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `$x Appreciation` | Yes | Use as a topical subdivision under individual art forms and headings for national and ethnic art. |
| `$x Attribution` |  | Use as a topical subdivision under individual art forms and headings for national or ethnic art. |
| `$x Catalogs` |  | Use as a topical subdivision under types of objects, including art objects, collectors' items, etc., for works about listings of those objects that have been produced, that are available or located at particular places, or that occur on a particular market, often systematically arranged with descriptive details, prices, etc., accompanying each entry. |
| `$x Conservation and restoration` | Yes | Use as a topical subdivision under types of art objects, etc., for works on preserving and restoring those items. |
| `$x Copying` |  | Use as a topical subdivision under individual art forms and headings for national or ethnic art. |
| `$x Expertising` | Yes | Use as a topical subdivision under headings for art forms and under types of art objects, types of architecture, and types of buildings. |
| `$x Foreign influences` |  | Not valid under period subdivisions. Use as a topical subdivision under art forms for works on general outside cultural influences on those topics. |
| `$x Forgeries` | Yes | Use as a topical subdivision under types of art objects, documents, etc. |
| `$x Influence` |  | Use as a topical subdivision under forms and movements in the visual arts for works discussing their influence. |
| `$x Reproduction` |  | Use as a topical subdivision under individual art forms and headings for national or ethnic art for the processes of producing images of the art. |
| `$x Technique` |  | Use under individual art forms and headings for national or ethnic art for works on artistic technique. |
| `$x Themes, motives` |  | Use as a topical subdivision under names of individual persons and individual literary and art forms. |

sections.heading: H. List of form subdivisions
sections.text:
LC practice: In 2026, the use of form subdivisions was phased out. Library of Congress catalogers assign Library of Congress Genre/Form Terms (LCGFT) to bring out the form(s) and/or genre(s) of the resource being cataloged. Therefore, the form subdivisions maintained on this list are not available for use by Library of Congress catalogers. Catalogers at institutions external to LC may use them as dictated by their own institutional policies.

| Subdivision | May Subd Geog | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `$v Catalogs` |  | Use as a form subdivision under types of objects, including types of merchandise, art objects, products, publications, collectors' items, technical equipment, etc., for listings of those objects that have been produced, that are available or located at particular places, or that occur on a particular market, often systematically arranged with descriptive details, prices, etc., accompanying each entry. |
| `$v Chronology` |  | Use as a form subdivision under headings for art for lists of dates of events pertinent to the subject in order of their occurrence. |
